policies.title: Jordan: named nationalities with visa issued on arrival
policies.summary: Jordan Tourism Board's live nationality table says these named nationalities may obtain a visa upon arrival.
conditions: Applies to the ordinary-passport, short-visitor baseline only; the table is nationality-specific and does not establish diplomatic, service, travel-pass, residence, work, transit or other special-document treatment.
The live table directly names Switzerland, Lithuania, Malaysia, Brunei, Kosovo, Belarus, Rwanda and South Sudan as Applicable and states that a visa can be obtained upon arrival.
The table also asks all non-Jordanians to obtain a Gateway2Jordan QR code before departure. That registration is not itself a visa or ETA and does not change this arrival-issuance classification.
The table does not establish port availability, duration, entries, waiver eligibility, security screening, final admission or other individual conditions.

policies.title: Jordan: named nationalities requiring a visa before arrival
policies.summary: Jordan Tourism Board's live nationality table directs these named nationalities to contact the closest Jordanian Embassy to obtain a visa before arrival.
conditions: Applies to the ordinary-passport, short-visitor baseline only; diplomatic, service, travel-pass, residence, work, transit and other special-document treatment are outside scope.
The live table directly names Colombia, Montenegro and Moldova as Not-Applicable for on-arrival issuance and directs the traveller to obtain a visa from the closest Jordanian Embassy before arrival.
The table does not establish duration, entries, fee, sponsor, security, final-admission or country-of-application conditions.

conflicts.explanation: Jordan Tourism Board's live Montenegro row says on-arrival issuance is Not-Applicable and directs obtaining a visa before arrival from the closest Jordanian Embassy.
Jordan Tourism Board's live Rwanda row says a visa can be obtained upon arrival, rather than visa-free entry.
Jordan Tourism Board's live South Sudan row says a visa can be obtained upon arrival, rather than requiring issuance before travel.
